title: An integrable density is a difference of two finite measures
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be any measure on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (σ-finiteness is not assumed), and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be μ-integrable. Then there are finite measures ν⁺ and ν⁻ on ℝ^P such that ∫ b dν⁺ − ∫ b dν⁻ = ∫ b g dμ for every Borel measurable function b : ℝ^P → ℝ that is bounded, i.e. |b(x)| ≤ C for some constant C and all x.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ), Integrable g μ → ∃ νpos νneg : Measure (Eucl P), IsFiniteMeasure νpos ∧ IsFiniteMeasure νneg ∧ ∀ b : Eucl P → ℝ, Measurable b → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, |b x| ≤ C) → ∫ x, b x ∂νpos - ∫ x, b x ∂νneg = ∫ x, b x * g x ∂μ
